Title: Spain ends national emergency for wildfires near Madrid
Article:
MADRID: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Thursday lifted the state of emergency over wildfires west of Madrid that forced the evacuations of tens of thousands of people.
Authorities said the fires in the Madrid and Avila areas had stopped spreading and there are "almost no flames", a week after the emergency was declared, mobilising a national firefighting effort.
"We decided to accept the proposal to switch to operational level 2 and end the national state of emergency," Sanchez told reporters after meeting with regional officials on the blazes.
The prefecture of the Madrid region said earlier in a statement that "night-time weather conditions have made it possible... to cool the area and reinforce the perimeter, which is clearly stabilised, with no spread for several days, few smoking spots and almost no flames left."
There were no longer any "active fronts," it said, adding that only around a thousand people remained evacuated.
But authorities warned that the ongoing heatwave threatened a resurgence of fire in the Madrid region.
The Madrid and Avila fires have jointly consumed at least 77,000 hectares (190,000 acres).
"The meteorological risk of fire remains very high, even extreme in some areas," the Madrid regional authority said.
[[nid:1500580]]
"Efforts will focus on maintaining the stability of the perimeter, monitoring for new outbreaks and cooling hot spots."
The most critical area in the Madrid region fires on Thursday morning was the area near the San Juan reservoir, about 60 kilometres from the centre of the capital, where two towns remained evacuated.
A new wildfire fire meanwhile broke out on Wednesday near Spain's border with Portugal, forcing the evacuation of more than 600 people, emergency services said.
A total of 11 areas were evacuated in the Fermoselle area, and residents of two others were ordered to shelter in place, the services said.
Authorities did not state the area burned, but several roads were closed.
Spain's Military Emergency Unit (UME) was deployed to the Level 2 fire – a classification that triggers extra support from the central government.
Two other Level 2 fires – at Val de la Loba and San Cipriano del Condado – were active in the same Zamora province.
The area is located in the Castile and Leon region, which has already been hit by the largest fire in Spanish history since record-keeping began.
That fire in Avila province, which is still ongoing, has burned approximately 50,000 hectares of land.

Title: Dewan Negara passes Social Work Profession Bill, establishes cross-sector council
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Negara today passed the Social Work Profession Bill 2026, which, among others, provides for the establishment of an inclusive Malaysian Social Work Profession Council comprising representatives from the government, private sector, non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and academia.
Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said the composition of the council is stipulated under Clause 3(2) of the Bill to ensure balance and inclusivity through representation from various sectors nationwide.
She said the council's leadership structure would be headed by the secretary-general of the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry as chairman, with the director-general of the Welfare Department serving as deputy chairman, enabling more effective cross-agency coordination.
Lim said the approach is also in line with international standards, such as those practised in Hong Kong, where decisions are made collectively by the council rather.
"We will have social workers from every state, as well as representatives from the public and private sectors. This means social work practitioners are assured of representation under the Act.
"In addition, the allocation for experts from the private sector provides broad opportunities for representatives of professional associations, NGOs, social work educators and academics to be appointed by the minister based on merit and expertise," she said when winding up the debate on the bill at its second reading in the Dewan Negara.
The bill was passed by a majority voice vote after being debated by 19 senators.
Lim said council members will be appointed for a term not exceeding two years to ensure expertise in the field can be fully utilised across various sectors.
She said the legislation is important to enhance the professionalism of the social work field, which is now facing increasingly complex social issues.
She said the bill provides for the establishment of the Malaysian Social Work Profession Council to regulate the registration of practitioners, set professional competency standards, and oversee the ethics and discipline of social workers.
"The bill is important to enable us to increase the number of qualified social workers in Malaysia from the private sector and NGOs who can work hand in hand with the government in providing social services to the people," she said.
She said the move would also protect the public from people who misuse the title of social worker without the necessary qualifications, while recognising the profession as an important career in strengthening the nation's social welfare ecosystem.
The sitting resumes on Monday.

Title: Philippines' Marcos approves release of VP Duterte's tax records to impeachment trial
Article:
MANILA: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has approved the release of Vice President Sara Duterte's tax records to the Senate in her impeachment trial, where one of the charges she is facing is that she has amassed unexplained wealth while in office.
"They can be opened, availed of by the parties as part of their evidence," Presidential Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro told Reuters in a message on Thursday.
Duterte's office did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Duterte has previously denied wrongdoing and called the impeachment proceedings politically motivated.
The Senate, which is sitting as the impeachment court, will resume Duterte's trial on Aug 3.
Under the law, presidential authorisation is required before the Bureau of Internal Revenue can release confidential tax records.
The Senate had issued a subpoena for Duterte's tax records but stopped short of ordering their release, saying disclosure must first comply with taxpayer confidentiality rules.
The Senate has also ordered banks and the Anti-Money Laundering Council to produce financial records related to Duterte and her husband.
Duterte is facing an impeachment trial over allegations of misuse of public funds, unexplained wealth, bribery, corruption, and threats against Marcos, the first lady and a former House speaker.
A conviction, which requires the votes of at least 16 of the Senate's 24 members, could derail Duterte's planned 2028 presidential bid.
Marcos and Duterte, ​scions of two of the country's most powerful political dynasties, ​ran on a joint ticket and won the 2022 election in a landslide but their alliance lapsed into acrimony.

Title: KTMB records strong growth in first half of 2026, revenue increases to RM296mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) recorded 13.2 million passengers in the first half of 2026, an increase of eight per cent compared to the same period last year.
Its group chief executive officer, Datuk Azlan Shah Al Bakri said the increase also contributed to the company's total revenue from RM206 million to RM296 million.
He said the growth was driven primarily by the excellent performance of the Electric Train Service (ETS), which recorded a 55 per cent increase in the number of passengers, from two million to 3.1 million, in addition to the Intercity service with 2.1 million passengers.
"This performance reflects the strong recovery of passenger services and KTMB's commitment to continuously improve reliability and the customer travel experience.
"Although KTMB is moving in the right direction, the fact is that we have not yet reached the targeted level," he said at a "Meet the Editor" session, which was also attended by Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) Editor-in-Chief, Arul Rajoo Durar Raj, here today.
Azlan Shah said that the KTM Komuter service is still facing challenges as the number of passengers decreased by four per cent in the first six months of this year compared to the same period last year.
He said the decline was due to operational disruptions following the closure of one track in the Salak Selatan-Seremban and Port Klang-KL Sentral sectors for the implementation of the Klang Valley Double Track Phase 2 (KVDT2) project, which in turn affected user confidence and fare revenue.
Meanwhile, Azlan Shah said the cargo segment also recorded positive performance as the volume of cargo increased to 887,000 tonnes compared to 724,000 tonnes in the same period last year, while container handling increased to 120,000 TEU (twenty-foot equivalent) from 108,000 TEU.
He said the growth in operations contributed to a 12 per cent increase in revenue to RM61.2 million compared to RM54.7 million previously, in addition to cargo movement through the Road-to-Rail initiative increasing by 16 per cent to 85,000 from 73,000.
"This achievement proves that the rail logistics sector has great potential to continue growing, while the Road-to-Rail Agenda not only enhances logistics efficiency but also reduces road congestion, accident risks and carbon emissions," he said.
Regarding the growth of passenger services, Azlan Shah said it is driven by a strategy to strengthen the north-south network and increase service capacity.
He said that since its introduction in December 2025, the direct ETS KL Sentral-JB Sentral service has recorded more than 638,445 passengers up to June 30, in addition to the reception of 10 new ETS sets, which has increased the service frequency from 22 to 44 trips per day.
In addition, the Southern Shuttle, which offers 14 daily trips connecting Kulai, Kempas Baru, JB Sentral and Pasir Gudang, recorded more than 2,712 passengers as of June 26, while the EMU Plus service for the Klang-KL Sentral-Ipoh route carried 42,801 passengers until last June.
Commenting on operational aspects, Azlan Shah said KTMB successfully reduced the number of operational disruptions by 27 per cent to 1,085 cases for the period from January to June compared to 1,494 cases in the same period last year.
He said the total minutes of disruption also decreased by 40 per cent to 113,431 minutes from 188,525 minutes, reflecting the effectiveness of the company's ongoing efforts to improve network reliability and operational performance.
However, he said, the main challenges that still affect the punctuality of services now mostly stem from cable theft, third-party disruptions, and external factors such as floods, fallen trees, and utility work near the tracks.
"KTMB will continue to strengthen asset monitoring, enhance cooperation with authorities, expedite the upgrading of the signaling system through KVDT, and reinforce operational readiness to ensure safer, more reliable and punctual services," he said.
Azlan Shah said that to strengthen the capacity of KTM Komuter services, they will receive 12 new train sets, with the first set in Completely Knocked Down (CKD) form to be received in August.
He said that the new commuter sets to be deployed for the KTM Komuter Utara service need to undergo technical testing, authorisation, safety certification, and trial runs to meet all operational and safety standards before being allowed to operate.
"This process usually takes quite a long time, in line with KTMB's commitment to ensure that every train it operates is safe, reliable and provides the best travel experience for passengers," he also said, adding that the train is expected to be put into service in February 2027.

Title: UPSI student clinches bronze at Adobe World Championship
Article:
TANJUNG MALIM: A Universiti Pendidikan Sultan Idris (UPSI) student brought pride to Malaysia when he finished third at the prestigious Adobe Certified Professional (ACP) World Championship in Anaheim, California.
Muhammad Fawwaz Haiqal Mohd Fuaad, a student at UPSI's Faculty of Computing and Meta Technology (Meta), beat 200 other participants from 45 countries in the international competition held yesterday.
The Education (Information Technology) undergraduate received a cash prize of US$2,000 for his achievement at the championship, organised by Certiport International, which challenges participants to produce creative poster designs using Adobe Photoshop, Illustrator and InDesign.
Fawwaz's success was achieved under the guidance of Ahmad Nurzid Rosli from the Meta Faculty's Computer Science and Digital Technology Department.
UPSI vice-chancellor Professor Datuk Dr Md Amin Md Taff said the achievement reflected not only Fawwaz's exceptional talent but also demonstrated the university's commitment to producing globally competitive digital professionals.
"His success places UPSI and Malaysia on the world map as a producer of high-calibre digital talent.
"UPSI will continue to nurture international-level digital talent through professional training and certification programmes.
"At the national level, we hope more institutions will collaborate to strengthen digital talent development and position Malaysia as a regional leader in digital creativity and innovation," he said in a statement.
Meanwhile, Malaysian contingent manager Natalie Sit described this year's edition as the country's best performance yet at the championship.
For the first time, Malaysia secured three major awards, with Fawwaz claiming third place, while Muhammad Nafiz Asyraaf Mohd Nazrin from Universiti Teknologi Mara (UiTM) Sarawak finished fourth and won the People's Choice Award.
The latest achievement also marks the fifth consecutive year that the Malaysian contingent has secured podium finishes at the prestigious ACP World Championship.

Title: Police cripple illegal Bitcoin mining operation in Batu Gajah
Article:
BATU GAJAH: Police have crippled an illegal Bitcoin mining operation in Tronoh, with the arrest of two men and the seizure of 73 cryptocurrency mining machines believed to have been powered by stolen electricity.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Md Noor Aehawan Mohammad said the raids were carried out at three premises at 9.02pm on Tuesday under Op Elektrik, following intelligence gathering and surveillance.
He said the operation involved officers from the district Criminal Investigation Department and Tenaga Nasional Bhd's (TNB) Technical Unit, also known as the SEAL Team.
"Investigations found that all three premises were carrying out Bitcoin mining activities using illegal electricity connections.
"Police arrested two men, aged 40 and 52, to assist in the investigation. We also seized 73 Bitcoin mining machines together with various equipment believed to have been used in the illegal operation," he said in a statement today.
He said technical inspections by TNB confirmed electricity theft at two abandoned houses, while the third premises was an unoccupied house.
"They have been remanded for three days, from Wednesday until tomorrow, to facilitate investigations," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 427 of the Penal Code for committing mischief, including electricity theft, and Section 37(1) of the Electricity Supply Act 1990 for tampering with electrical installations.
He reminded the public to remain vigilant and report any suspicious activities in their residential areas.
He urged those with information on illegal electricity theft or cryptocurrency mining activities to contact the Batu Gajah district police operations room at 05-362 9222 or the nearest police station.

Title: Anwar congratulates Aliff Rakib on ONE Muay Thai world title win
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated Muay Thai fighter Aliff Rakib on his historic achievement of becoming the first Malaysian to win the ONE Interim Muay Thai Strawweight World Championship.
Anwar said he received Aliff at his office and congratulated him on the milestone.
He said the victory had not only brought pride to Malaysia on the international stage but also demonstrated that young Malaysians possess the ability, discipline and fighting spirit to compete with the world's best.
"May this achievement inspire more young people to continue pursuing their dreams with determination, commitment and efforts that never know the meaning of giving up.
"Congratulations Aliff, Malaysia is proud of this achievement," he said in a Facebook post today.

Title: MACC forms task force to review Tabung Haji RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has formed a special task force to review the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) following its public release.
MACC said its Investigation Division senior director Datuk Mohd Hafaz Nazar had been appointed to lead the special task force.
"The RCI report, which was published on the official Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim) portal on July 29, will be examined for any legal issues involving corruption, criminal breach of trust, document forgery, abuse of power, money laundering or other related offences.
"The team will scrutinise the report for any offences under the MACC Act, the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act, or any other relevant laws," MACC said in a statement.

Title: Trust: New currency of the AI era
Article:
UNLIKE previous technological revolutions, artificial intelligence (AI) is not simply changing how we work. It is beginning to influence how we think, decide, create, govern and trust.
That distinction makes artificial intelligence not merely a technology agenda but a national governance agenda.
Malaysia's decision to establish AI Malaysia to drive the country's ambitions towards 2030 therefore deserves recognition as a strategically significant step.
It demonstrates an understanding that AI cannot remain a collection of isolated initiatives scattered across ministries and industries. It requires national coordination, policy coherence and long-term commitment.
Yet institutions alone do not build AI nations. Trust does.
The nations that will lead the AI era are unlikely to be those with the largest computing power alone. They will be those that build the strongest relationship between innovation, ethics and public trust.
Artificial intelligence is not arriving in a vacuum. It enters a world already confronting declining institutional trust, information disorder, geopolitical uncertainty and an increasingly sceptical public.
Against that backdrop, every AI policy is also a communications challenge.
Every algorithm that influences a financial decision, every AI-assisted medical diagnosis, every automated legal review and every government service powered by machine learning raises a fundamental question that no software engineer can answer alone:
Why should people trust it? The answer will not be found in code. It will be found in transparency, accountability and communication.
The healthcare sector illustrates both the promise and the complexity of this new era.
Artificial intelligence is already assisting clinicians in detecting cancers earlier, analysing radiological images with greater speed, predicting patient deterioration and accelerating pharmaceutical research. These advances have the potential to redefine public health outcomes.
Yet medicine has never been merely a science of diagnosis. It is equally a profession of empathy, ethics and human judgement.
Patients do not place their trust in algorithms. They place their trust in professionals who use technology responsibly.
The legal profession faces an equally profound transformation.
Artificial intelligence can now conduct legal research in minutes, analyse thousands of pages of contracts, identify precedent and assist in litigation strategy. These capabilities will reshape legal practice by removing repetitive tasks and increasing efficiency.
But justice has never been determined by information alone.
Law requires interpretation, proportionality, ethics and an understanding of human circumstance.
These are qualities that remain uniquely human. The future belongs not to lawyers who compete against AI, but to lawyers who combine tech fluency with wisdom, judgement and integrity.
Financial services present perhaps the clearest example of AI's duality.
Banks increasingly depend on AI to detect fraud, strengthen cybersecurity, improve compliance, personalise financial services and enhance risk management.
Machine learning is becoming embedded in decisions involving lending, investment and insurance.
Yet finance has always operated on a single currency more valuable than capital itself: confidence.
A single opaque algorithm, an unexplained bias in automated lending, or a significant AI-driven security breach can erode public confidence built over decades.
Financial institutions that prosper in the AI economy will not necessarily be those with the most sophisticated models. They will be those that remain the most trusted.
No profession, however, is likely to undergo a more immediate identity shift than communications.
Much attention has focused on whether generative AI will write press releases, speeches, articles and social media content. This framing fundamentally misunderstands the profession.
Public relations has never been in the business of producing words. It has been in the business of producing understanding.
AI can generate language with extraordinary speed. It can summarise reports, identify patterns, monitor sentiment and recommend responses.
What it cannot do is replace human judgement during a national crisis, negotiate competing stakeholder interests, counsel chief executives through ethical dilemmas or understand the political, cultural and emotional context in which decisions are made.
In an age of synthetic media, deepfakes and algorithmically amplified misinformation, communications professionals become even more essential — not less.
Their role evolves from content producers to custodians of trust. Engineers, doctors, lawyers, auditors, educators, regulators and corporate leaders will increasingly find that technical competence alone is no longer sufficient.
Every profession must now acquire fluency in ethics, governance and public accountability alongside technological capability.
This is why AI Malaysia should be viewed not simply as a technology initiative but as a nation-building initiative.
Its ultimate success should not be measured by the number of memoranda signed, investment commitments secured or computing facilities constructed.
The true measure of success will be whether artificial intelligence shortens hospital waiting times, strengthens educational outcomes, improves agricultural productivity, supports small and medium enterprises, modernises public services and expands economic opportunity without compromising privacy, fairness or human dignity.
That is the social contract AI must fulfil.
Malaysia has an opportunity to distinguish itself not by attempting to outspend larger economies, but by becoming one of the world's most trusted AI ecosystems — one that demonstrates that innovation and ethics are not competing priorities but mutually reinforcing ones.
If we succeed, Malaysia will not merely adopt artificial intelligence. We will demonstrate how a diverse, plural and developing nation can harness it responsibly.
As Malaysia advances towards its 2030 ambitions, our greatest competitive advantage will not be artificial intelligence itself.
It will be our collective intelligence to govern it wisely, communicate it transparently and ensure that innovation never outpaces public confidence.
Because, in the end, artificial intelligence will not define Malaysia. Trust will.
* The writer is Deputy Chairman, Public Relations Practitioners Society of Malaysia (PRactitioners) & AI Communications advocate

Title: Negri polls: Vote-buying allegations unfair, says Aminuddin
Article:
PORT DICKSON: Negri Sembilan Pakatan Harapan chairman Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun has described allegations linking the coalition to vote-buying as unfair.
He said such accusations should not be directed at any single political party, as no one knows who was behind the alleged vote-buying.
"Until now, we do not know who carried out the vote-buying. I think Datuk Jalal's (Datuk Seri
Jalaluddin Alias
) accusation yesterday should not be directed at a single political party.
"As of today, we still do not know who did it," he said when met here today.
Aminuddin, who is also Negri Sembilan caretaker menteri besar, said vote-buying should not occur during an election.
"I understand that several parties have lodged reports regarding this matter, and it may now be under police investigation.
"We cannot categorically say it came from a particular party because it could have been a non-governmental organisation or some other party.
"I myself saw the viral information yesterday. Based on that picture, I too could make accusations. If we keep accusing one another, the matter will never be resolved. It is better to investigate and produce evidence," he said.
Earlier, Jalaluddin, who is Negri Sembilan Umno liaison committee chairman, said a source had informed him of the alleged incident.
He said the same thing was believed to have occurred at several other locations and had also circulated on social media.

Title: Anwar lauds Maybank's transformation into regional banking leader
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has praised Maybank's transformation into one of Asia's leading financial institutions.
He said the bank's success is underpinned not only by strong financial performance but also by sound governance and integrity.
Speaking at the opening of Maybank's new headquarters, Menara Merdeka Maybank, today, Anwar described the banking group as a national landmark and a symbol of Malaysia's economic progress.
He congratulated Maybank's leadership, employees and past contributors, saying the institution's achievements were the result of decades of dedication, hard work and commitment.
"Maybank is a tower that reflects the country's success, a proud landmark and a strong financial institution recognised across Asia."
Anwar said Maybank's strength stemmed not only from its expertise, innovation and financial capabilities but also from its commitment to integrity and responsible management.
He said financial institutions worldwide, including those in Malaysia, continued to face challenges related to integrity, governance and responsible management.
"These values are easy to promote as slogans, but much harder to practise because human nature can sometimes be drawn towards actions that undermine institutions."
Anwar, who is also the finance minister, said Maybank's reputation was built not merely on financial achievements but also on its high professional standards and governance practices.
"Maybank remains strong not only because of its financial performance but also because of its excellent governance and services."
He urged Maybank to maintain these standards as it navigates future challenges, including rapid technological advances such as artificial intelligence and quantum computing.
Anwar also highlighted Maybank's role in supporting Malaysia's economic development, saying the government's efforts to strengthen the economy had benefited from close cooperation with financial institutions.
He expressed confidence that Maybank would continue contributing to a more inclusive and sustainable economy while maintaining its position as a leading regional banking group.
The event also marked the official opening of Menara Merdeka Maybank ahead of Malaysia's 67th Merdeka celebrations.
Also present were Maybank president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli; Maybank Group chairman Tan Sri Zamzamzairani Mohd Isa; Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar; and Finance Minister II Amir Hamzah Azizan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jamil Khir says TH decisions were based on board recommendations
Article:
SEREMBAN: Former Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom said he never acted beyond the investment recommendations submitted by the Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) Board during his tenure overseeing the institution from 2009 to 2018.
Jamil Khir said TH operates under the government's governance framework and that the minister cannot approve any application, request, sale or purchase of assets, or leasing matters unless they are first recommended by TH.
He said TH is also prohibited from making any proposal unless it has first been reviewed by its risk management team to ensure compliance with good governance practices and syariah principles.
"That is why I am very confident. During the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into TH, I said, 'Please review every memorandum submitted to me and identify any instance where I acted beyond the recommendations brought forward by the board.
"The minister's authority is based on the board's recommendations," he said.
Jamil Khir, who is also an Umno Supreme Council member, said this when met after the launch of the Negri Sembilan Pledge by the Barisan Nasional Women's Wing here today.
Jamil Khir was asked about the RCI report on TH released yesterday and the commission's finding that the minister responsible for TH was vested with extensive powers under the Tabung Haji Act 1995, covering almost every aspect of the institution's governance, management and operations.
Jamil Khir, who was also among the witnesses called by the RCI, said TH's governance had been audited by the National Audit Department, as well as international audit firms, and had received clean audit reports from 2009 to 2017.
"Although some people spoke about embezzlement, theft and misappropriation of funds, the RCI found no such findings or allegations.
"What it did find was a report made in 2017 stating that our financial assets were lower than our liabilities. That is why they said there was an amount that was considered inappropriate to be paid out.
"I hope the public will fully understand that TH, which was established in 1963, is governed and regulated under the Tabung Haji Act," he said.
Asked whether he was prepared to be investigated by the authorities, Jamil Khir said he had no issue if called in and had gone through the process before.
"If they want to investigate, go ahead. I'm not going to run away. I'm a Malaysian citizen," he said.
Yesterday, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim ordered a comprehensive investigation into any elements of abuse of power or legal breaches following the release of the RCI report on TH.
He said the investigation would involve the police, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission and Bank Negara Malaysia.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rais Yatim accepts withdrawal of Negri honours with 'open heart'
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Negri Sembilan menteri besar Tan Sri Rais Yatim has accepted the withdrawal of two Negri Sembilan honours "with an open heart".
In a video posted on TikTok by @minaq_jinggo, Rais said he had received notification that the Negri Sembilan palace had withdrawn the Datuk Seri Utama and Datuk honours today.
"I accept it with an open heart and with my usual philosophy of life.
"Seasons change and honours are conferred. There is a time when honours are bestowed, and there is a time when they are taken back," he said.
Rais said both honours were conferred on him in 1982 after he stepped down as menteri besar.
He said they were bestowed by the late Tuanku Ja'afar ibni Almarhum Tuanku Abdul Rahman in recognition of his service as menteri besar at the time.
He also urged the public not to politicise the matter or regard it as an attack during the ongoing state election campaign.
"I appeal to those who think further and with the best of intentions not to regard this as an attack during the election period, and not to use it as an issue to target any party.
"As for whether it was wise for this notice to be issued at this particular time, namely on July 30, I leave that to the people of Negri Sembilan, particularly the voters in Klawang and Jelebu," he said.
Rais said the withdrawal of honours was not unprecedented, adding that former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, the late former Johor menteri besar Tan Sri Osman Saat and the country's 10th prime minister had also experienced similar situations.
"It is neither a matter of concern nor a major issue. Honours are conferred and honours are withdrawn," said Rais, who previously served as Dewan Negara president and held several Cabinet positions.
On the reason for the withdrawal, Rais said it was not for him to explain.
"The public may ask what the reason is. That is not for me to answer. Those who have been involved in this matter should provide the explanation," he said.
When contacted by the New Straits Times, Rais confirmed that the video statement was authentic.
Earlier today, the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan revoked
two state honour
s conferred on Rais with immediate effect.
Registrar of Orders Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim said Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir had decreed the withdrawal of the Darjah Seri Utama, conferred in 2001, and the Darjah Dato' Setia, awarded in 1979.
He said the decision was made to preserve the dignity, prestige and honour of the Negri Sembilan royal institution.
The Darjah Seri Utama carries the title Datuk Seri Utama, while the Darjah Dato' Setia carries the title Datuk.
Rais was conferred the Panglima Setia Mahkota (PSM) federal title, which carries the title Tan Sri, in 2013.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man pleads not guilty over foster mother's RM182,223 account misuse
Article:
ROMPIN: A food stall helper pleaded not guilty at the Magistrate's Court here today to charges of dishonestly using RM182,223 from his foster mother's account, as well as unlawfully possessing her debit card.
Mohamad Nor Farazul Mohamed, 37, who faces four charges, including two related to drug offences, entered his plea before magistrate Melody Woon Sze Mun.
Nor Farazul was accused of possessing a bank debit card belonging to a 69-year-old woman without lawful authority on July 28 at a stall in Taman Seri Maulana, Pekan.
He was charged under Section 424A of the Penal Code for fraud, which carries a maximum jail term of five years, a fine of up to RM50,000, or both upon conviction.
For the second charge, he was accused of dishonestly misusing RM182,223 belonging to the same individual by using her debit card without her knowledge between April 1 and June 20 this year in Pekan.
The charge, framed under Section 403 of the Penal Code, carries a jail term of between six months and five years, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Kamisah Ismail prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer Ahmad Deniel Roslan.
The court set bail at RM10,000 for both charges and fixed Sept 21 for mention.
Meanwhile, Nor Farazul pleaded guilty to two other charges involving possession of 5.65g of methamphetamine and self-administering the prohibited substance.
The alleged offences were committed at a house in Pekan and at the Pekan police headquarters respectively between 3.10pm and 4.35pm yesterday.
He was charged under Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 for possessing the drugs. If convicted, he may be sentenced to imprisonment of not less than two years and shall be liable to not less than three strokes of the cane.
For the fourth charge under Section 15(1)(a) of the same Act, he faces a fine of up to RM5,000 or imprisonment of up to two years, as well as supervision for between two and three years upon conviction.
The court fixed bail at RM1,500 and RM5,000 for the third and fourth charges respectively, and fixed Sept 21 for mention. The accused was unable to raise the bail amounts and was sent to Penor Prison.

Title: Bursa backs expanding FBM KLCI to 50 constituents
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Bhd has backed a proposal to expand the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) from 30 to 50 constituents in a move to better reflect the breadth of the domestic equity market.
The proposal, issued jointly by Bursa Malaysia and global index provider FTSE Russell for market consultation, forms part of a broader review of the methodology for the FBM KLCI and the FTSE Bursa Malaysia Mid 70 Index (FBM70).
Chief executive officer Datuk Fad'l Mohamed said the expansion would broaden market coverage, strengthen sector representation and reduce concentration risks, particularly in the financial services sector.
Currently, the 30 FBM KLCI constituents account for about 59 per cent of the Main Market's total market capitalisation. Expanding the index to 50 constituents would increase that coverage to around 70 per cent.
"The main objective of this proposal is to enhance sector representation and reduce concentration risks in certain sectors, particularly financial services," he said at a briefing on Bursa Malaysia's first-half 2026 financial performance today.
The financial services sector currently accounts for about 43 per cent of the FBM KLCI.
Under the proposal, its weighting is expected to decline to the mid-30 per cent range, allowing greater representation from sectors such as technology, energy and real estate investment trusts.
Separately, Fad'l said foreign investors have returned to Malaysian equities as global market rotations continue following a correction in regional technology stocks.
Malaysia recorded positive foreign inflows in July, with investors returning to sectors such as banking and utilities, which offer stable dividend yields.
"Markets continue to be rotational. Recently, we saw very high activities and flows into markets such as Taiwan and South Korea, driven by technology-related stocks and technology-related growth.
"As we have seen some correction in technology-related stocks, we are now seeing flows coming back to Malaysia," he said.
He said Malaysia continues to offer investors diversification opportunities, supported by a balanced investor base comprising retail investors, domestic institutions and foreign institutions.

Title: Ayob Khan on the Nicky Liow investigation: "It was one of Bukit Aman's biggest cases"
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Few investigations left as deep an impression on former deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay as the "Gang Nicky" probe.
So deeply involved was he in the case that it earned a special mention in his recently launched book, 'Dari Pendang ke Bukit Aman'.
In the chapter 'Bukit Aman and Greater Trust' Ayob revisits one of the most complex and high-profile investigations of his policing career.
The recently retired police was the leader of an investigation involving Nicky Liow when he was the Johor police chief.
Liow was later charged but eventually
acquitted of 26 money laundering charges
involving more than RM36 million after the prosecution withdrew the case four years ago.
"It was one of the biggest cases and attracted significant public attention," Ayob said when asked why the case was highlighted in the book.
[[nid:1500575]]
The case involving Liow became a defining moment in Ayob's fight against organised crime as it was not merely a police operation, but a test of leadership, courage and institutional integrity.
The investigation began with three police reports involving what appeared to be routine online fraud cases. Victims had lodged reports after discovering missing funds and misuse of their bank accounts.
However, to investigators, the reports pointed towards a much larger operation involving complex financial transactions and a structured network.
An officer from the Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID), then holding the rank of assistant superintendent, later briefed Ayob on the initial findings.
From the briefing, it became apparent that the case was not an isolated fraud matter. It involved a flow of funds, an extensive network and layers of financial accounts that required deeper investigation.
The operation later saw a raid at Trigon Residence, SetiaWalk, Puchong, where 45 condominium units were searched based on intelligence and reasonable grounds, according to Ayob.
The investigation revealed how modern criminal networks could operate behind the façade of legitimate businesses, corporate structures and affluent lifestyles.
The case also raised concerns over alleged involvement of enforcement personnel. Ayob had previously revealed that several officers and members of enforcement agencies were suspected of having links to the syndicate.
During Ops Pelican 3.0 Phase 2, 12 enforcement officers — comprising 10 police personnel and two Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officers — were detained in Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, Melaka and Negeri Sembilan.
They were remanded for 28 days under the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (SOSMA), with investigations conducted under provisions related to organised crime under the Penal Code.
[[nid:1500574]]
For Ayob, rank and position could not be used as protection from scrutiny.
He maintained that betrayal within enforcement agencies was a serious offence, as those entrusted with upholding the law had allegedly become linked to the very networks they were supposed to combat.
The case highlighted the challenge of tackling organised crime, where internal threats could be more difficult to detect as individuals familiar with the system could exploit weaknesses, delay investigations or compromise information.
The investigation also demonstrated that combating financial crime required more than raids and arrests. It involved extensive document analysis, scrutiny of financial records, cooperation with financial institutions and following the movement of funds.
On April 9, 2021, Liow and his brother were charged in the Petaling Jaya Sessions Court for allegedly being members of an organised crime group. Liow was charged in absentia.
However, Liow voluntarily surrendered to the police on April 11, 2022. He was charged with 26 money laundering charges the next day.
[[nid:1500573]]
On July 7, the same year, the Court of Appeal acquitted and discharged 14 accused, including Liow's two younger brothers from charges of being involved in the organised crime group.
This is after the A-GC had received representations from all appellants to be fully acquitted of the charges.
On July 24, 2023, Liow's younger brother Liow Wei Kin was also freed from tax evasion and money laundering charges after he paid RM4.147 million worth of unpaid taxes, special penalty, fine and compound for his money laundering charges.
Liow, who is the founder of Winner Dynasty Group, had been tracked down by the police over a Macau Scam syndicate after 68 of its members were arrested in "Op Pelican 3.0" in March 2021.
On April 26, the same year, the Pahang palace stripped Liow of the Darjah Kebesaran Darjah Sri Sultan Ahmad Shah Pahang (SSAP) which carries the title of Datuk Seri.
Liow recently made headlines after a photograph of him wearing a PKR shirt alongside party president and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim surfaced online, sparking speculation over the status of his court case.
On July 26, PKR secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh denied that Liow was a party member, saying there was no record of him having applied for membership.
On Wednesday, Liow accompanied by his lawyer Datuk Rajpal Singh held a press conference and told reporters that the PKR Youth shirt he wore was given to him and did not indicate any affiliation with the party.
Rajpal also made it clear to reporters that his client had never been convicted of any crime and had successfully fought all his legal battles.

Title: MSMEs GDP grows 5.7pct in 2025, outpaces overall economy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) gross domestic product (GDP) grew 5.7 per cent in 2025, outpacing the country's overall GDP growth of 5.2 per cent, according to the Statistics Department.
In its Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 2025 publication released today, the department said MSMEs' value added rose to RM689.8 billion in 2025 from RM652.8 billion in 2024, accounting for 39.7 per cent of Malaysia's GDP.
It attributed the stronger performance to government initiatives under the 2025 Budget, including financing facilities, incentives and entrepreneur development programmes aimed at boosting productivity, accelerating digitalisation, technology adoption and innovation, and expanding market access for MSMEs.
The services and manufacturing sectors remained the largest contributors to MSMEs' GDP, accounting for a combined 84.5 per cent, followed by agriculture (8.4 per cent), construction (5.3 per cent) and mining and quarrying (0.5 per cent).
At the sectoral level, the services sector grew 5.7 per cent in 2025, unchanged from the previous year.
Growth in the sector was driven by wholesale and retail trade, food and beverage, and accommodation activities (5.0 per cent); finance, insurance, real estate and business services (6.6 per cent); and transportation and storage, and information and communication (7.7 per cent).
The manufacturing sector expanded 4.8 per cent in 2025, easing from 5.0 per cent in 2024, supported by growth in food, beverages and tobacco (9.6 per cent); other manufacturing (4.7 per cent); and non-metallic mineral products, basic metals and fabricated metal products (4.7 per cent).
Meanwhile, the agriculture sector grew 1.8 per cent in 2025, slowing from 3.1 per cent in 2024, mainly supported by the rubber, oil palm, livestock and other agriculture sub-sectors, which expanded 2.3 per cent.
The construction sector grew 12.0 per cent in 2025, compared with 17.5 per cent a year earlier, while mining and quarrying expanded 4.4 per cent, against 4.8 per cent in 2024.
MSMEs' exports rose 10.5 per cent to RM214.5 billion in 2025, compared with growth of 29.5 per cent in 2024.
The increase was driven by manufacturing and services exports, which grew 8.8 per cent (2024: 7.9 per cent) and 14.0 per cent (2024: 106.6 per cent), respectively.
MSMEs accounted for 14.7 per cent of Malaysia's total exports in 2025. Manufacturing remained the largest contributor, followed by services and agriculture.
Manufacturing exports by MSMEs increased to RM132.7 billion in 2025 from RM122.0 billion in 2024.

Title: Anwar calls for banks to 'humanise' financial services
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on financial institutions to go beyond profitability by ensuring greater access to quality financial services for all Malaysians.
Anwar said financial institutions must embrace the concept of "humanising financial services" by balancing commercial success with social responsibility.
He said financial services should not only benefit businesses and wealthy segments of society but must also reach ordinary Malaysians, including those from lower-income groups.
"What is democracy? It is not only about voting during elections.
"Democracy means democratisation of access; access to quality services, financial services and education," he said at the opening of Maybank's new headquarters at Menara Merdeka Maybank today.
The finance minister said that without such access, development would only benefit a limited group while leaving vulnerable communities behind.
He said financial institutions had traditionally focused on meeting business needs and generating profits, but in a modern and independent nation, they must also play a role in ensuring broader participation in economic growth.
"This is why we must give meaning to humanising financial services, by bringing humanity into the system and ensuring people benefit from progress."
Anwar also praised Maybank's "humanising financial services" initiative, saying financial institutions could make a difference by combining profit-making objectives with empathy and trust.
He said Malaysia's financial institutions must continue to strengthen their role in supporting inclusive growth while maintaining sound economic fundamentals.
Anwar also highlighted Malaysia's recent economic performance, saying the country recorded 5.8 per cent growth in the second quarter, alongside strong investment levels, low unemployment and controlled inflation.
He said financial institutions remained a key pillar in supporting Malaysia's economic development and must continue to uphold good governance and integrity.
Present at the launch were Maybank president and group chief executive officer Datuk Seri Khairussaleh Ramli, Maybank Group chairman Tan Sri Zamzamzairani Mohd Isa, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Finance Minister II Amir Hamzah Azizan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Starlink eyes Malaysia for direct-to-cell internet trial
Article:
CYBERJAYA: Telecommunications giant Starlink is looking to conduct trials of its direct-to-device satellite internet technology in Malaysia.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said this could potentially expand internet access to areas without telecommunications towers, particularly sparsely populated locations.
"Representatives from Starlink recently met with me to brief me on a service they intend to trial in Malaysia on a pilot basis, namely direct-to-device, or direct-to-cell, technology.
"This is a significant technological advancement because it means we can provide internet connectivity via satellite to certain areas that do not have telecommunications towers, particularly locations with low population density," he said.
Fahmi said this at a memorandum of understanding exchange ceremony between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission and the Malaysian Highway Authority.
Last year, however, Fahmi had said Putrajaya was
exploring alternative options
to reduce its reliance on Starlink's low-earth orbit satellite internet service, operated by SpaceX, the company founded by billionaire Elon Musk.

Title: 77 telco towers planned to boost highway coverage
Article:
CYBERJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will build 77 telecommunications towers along 50km of highway stretches nationwide identified as having poor mobile coverage.
Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the initiative is part of the government's broader commitment to developing smart highways in the country.
"MCMC is targeting the construction of 77 new telecommunications towers along 50km of highway stretches identified as having unsatisfactory coverage," he said at the memorandum of understanding (MoU) exchange ceremony between MCMC and the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) today.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who also attended the ceremony, said MCMC had issued a tender on May 15 to improve internet coverage through the construction of telecommunications towers along 10 MHA-managed highways with weak connectivity.
The highways include the East Coast Expressway 2, the West Coast Expressway, and geographically challenging locations such as the Menora Tunnel and Gua Tempurung along the North-South Expressway.
Fahmi said the MoU would also strengthen the country's digital infrastructure to support future mobility technologies such as the Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) toll collection system and Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS), both of which require stable and reliable network connectivity.
The collaboration between the Communications Ministry and the Works Ministry aims to improve communications access for motorists throughout their journeys, including emergency communications, navigation services, real-time traffic information and other digital services, through the deployment of telecommunications towers and fibre optic networks.
The initiative is also expected to enhance road safety and convenience by addressing weak coverage areas, or blind spots, that frequently result in dropped calls, through the use of highway reserve land, or Right of Way (ROW), for communications infrastructure.

Title: New UK PM urged to put food on a par with defence and energy
Article:
LONDON: A fresh food shock in Britain is only a matter of time after years of disruptions that have driven up prices, more than 100 organisations said in a letter urging new Prime Minister Andy Burnham to make food a national priority alongside defence and energy.
Signatories, including food retailers Tesco and Sainsbury's and dairy producer Danone, called on Burnham to urgently introduce a "Good Food Bill" to improve food security, resilience and public health.
The letter, published on Thursday, said Britain's food system had suffered repeated shocks in recent years, with farmers and growers facing rising costs and increasing pressure from climate change and nature loss.
It noted that together, these pressures are contributing to higher food prices, which are forecast to be 50 per cent higher by November than at the start of Britain's cost of living crisis in 2021, according to research by the Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit.
"The next food shock is not a question of if, but when. To meet it prepared, food has to stop being an afterthought for the Government," the letter, organised by charity the Food Foundation, said.
It warned that wildfires across Europe and heightened geopolitical tensions had exposed the fragility of the UK's food system, while diet-related disease had reached record levels.
The proposed legislation would create a legal framework for food policy, including targets to reduce childhood obesity, increase fruit and vegetable consumption, boost the proportion of produce grown in Britain and cut household food insecurity.
Other signatories included retailers Aldi, the Co-op and Waitrose, food producer Greencore and investment company Rathbones.
In May, the UK government led by then prime minister Keir Starmer ruled out mandatory supermarket price caps, but said it was ‌in talks with the sector on ways to ease cost-of-living pressures partly driven by the Iran war.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Estate planning key to protecting family wealth, say experts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Estate planning should no longer be viewed as a tool reserved for the wealthy, with legal and financial experts urging Malaysians to start planning earlier to protect their families, preserve wealth and avoid future disputes.
They said changing family structures, increasing cross-border investments, digital assets and a growing intergenerational wealth transfer make estate planning more important than ever.
Estate planning for everyone
Malaysia Law Institution founder and Messrs Sim & Rahman Advocates and Solicitors, senior partner Sim Wen Yee said estate planning is relevant to everyone, regardless of their income or the size of their assets.
"It is about ensuring our loved ones are protected, our wishes are respected and potential disputes can be avoided in the future.
"Estate planning goes beyond drafting a will. It also includes trusts, hibah, powers of attorney and succession planning," she said.
Changing public perceptions
Sim said one of the biggest challenges facing the industry over the next decade would be encouraging younger Malaysians to begin planning before accumulating substantial wealth.
She said many people still believed estate planning was only necessary later in life, despite increasing cases involving family disputes and unclaimed assets.
Sim said continuous public education and collaboration among industry players would be key to changing that perception.
She said initiatives such as the Joint Global Business Conference (JGBC) 2026, organised by the Malaysia Law Institution and co-organised by AmanahRaya, provide a platform for professionals from the legal, financial, trust and wealth management sectors to exchange knowledge and strengthen the estate planning ecosystem.
Breaking common misconceptions
Meanwhile, AmanahRaya acting group managing director and group chief business and operating officer Jack Yap Ngee Heong said misconceptions remained one of the biggest obstacles preventing Malaysians from planning their estates.
"Many people think legacy planning is only for the wealthy or the elderly. In reality, anyone who owns assets or has loved ones depending on them should plan ahead.
"Many also believe there is always more time. Unfortunately, delaying the process can create uncertainty and make matters more difficult for family members," he said.
Yap said early planning provides greater flexibility in protecting assets and ensuring wealth is transferred according to the owner's wishes.
"Legacy planning is not just about passing on wealth. It is about preserving family harmony, protecting the people you care about and ensuring your wishes are carried out as intended."
He added that AmanahRaya continues to expand its services to meet the changing needs of younger Malaysians, many of whom now own businesses, investment portfolios and digital assets.
Besides wills and trusts, the organisation also provides corporate trustee services while making estate planning more accessible and easier to understand.
Cross-border wealth challenges
On cross-border wealth planning, JTC Kensington Labuan Limited associate director June Chin said growing international investments and migration had increased demand for more sophisticated estate planning structures.
JTC Kensington Labuan Limited is the Platinum Sponsor for this conference for the Joint Global Business Conference (JGBC) 2026.
She said Labuan Foundations offered a flexible solution for families with assets spread across multiple jurisdictions by providing clear governance and succession arrangements.
"Labuan Foundation has its own legal personality, allowing it to own and manage assets while preserving family wealth and ensuring continuity across generations.
"It combines features of both a trust and a company, making it suitable for long-term wealth preservation and orderly succession planning," she said.
June said clients were increasingly seeking governance structures that extended beyond wealth preservation to include family constitutions, succession principles and long-term stewardship.
She added that managing wealth across multiple jurisdictions also required close collaboration among lawyers, tax advisers, fiduciary specialists and investment professionals to address differing legal and regulatory requirements.
"Successful estate planning is built on collaboration. Professional advisers need to adopt a holistic approach to ensure wealth structures remain effective, compliant and aligned with each family's evolving needs," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maybank launches Menara Merdeka headquarters [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's largest bank, Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), has officially launched its new headquarters at Menara Merdeka Maybank, officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Maybank said the new headquarters reflects its commitment to the future by bringing its corporate functions under one roof.
It is designed to foster greater collaboration, innovation and operational excellence, enabling the bank to better serve the evolving needs of its customers and communities across the region.
Speaking at the ceremony, Anwar described the tower as a symbol of Malaysia's progress and a landmark of national pride.
"Maybank remains a strong financial institution, recognised across Asia, supported by the people of Malaysia, and has earned its place as one of the region's most respected financial institutions," he said in a speech.
Anwar said financial institutions must continue to uphold integrity, good governance and accountable management, noting that these principles are often easier to advocate than to practise.
Referring to the government's decision to release the Royal Commission of Inquiry report on Tabung Haji, Anwar said the pilgrimage fund's past challenges underscored the importance of sound governance and ethical leadership.
He said although the fund had built a distinguished legacy serving hundreds of thousands of pilgrims, it had nearly collapsed due to negligence, poor stewardship, greed and mismanagement.
However, the issues were detected early, and corrective measures enabled the institution to recover.
"The central issue remains integrity anchored in good governance, and producing professionals with the skills, expertise, integrity and dignity to uphold our institutions," he said.
Meanwhile, Maybank chairman Tan Sri Zamzamzairani Mohd Isa said the relocation reflects the bank's confidence in its future.
"It is guided by strong values, underpinned by sound governance, and committed to creating sustainable value for our customers, communities and the nation.
"Since its establishment in 1960, Maybank has grown alongside Malaysia's development.
"Through various changes and challenges, we have remained steadfast in upholding the values of integrity, excellence and trust, which have formed the foundation of this institution's strength," he said.
On Tuesday, Menara Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur was officially renamed Menara Merdeka Maybank, reflecting the bank's presence at the tower.
Its former headquarters on Jalan Tun Perak, previously known as Menara Maybank, will be renamed Menara Tun Perak following the relocation of the bank's headquarters.

Article:

Title: Ukraine targets Russia online retailer facilities
Article:
MOSCOW: Two warehouses belonging to the Russian online retail giant Wildberries, were targeted overnight by new Ukrainian drone attacks, the company and local authorities said Thursday.
One person was injured and more than 200 employees were evacuated after a drone attack sparked a fire in a Wildberries warehouse in the western Penza region, according to the regional governor, Oleg Melnichenko.
"Logistics chains have been reorganised; the receipt of goods and the dispatch of orders are being carried out at other sites," Wildberries said in a statement.
Another Wildberries warehouse was hit by a Ukrainian drone in Sarapul, about 1,100 km (685 miles) east of Moscow, and a fire broke out, according to the company.
Staff were evacuated and "according to preliminary information, no one was injured," Wildberries said
Ukraine first targeted Wildberries warehouses on July 18-19 in the Tambov region about 480 km southeast of the Russian capital, as well as in the Moscow region, resulting in eight casualties and destroying facilities.
Since then, Ukraine has launched attacks on a number of the company's warehouses around the country.
More than four years after the launch of Russia's large-scale offensive against Ukraine, diplomacy is at a standstill and both countries are ramping up their long-range strikes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Anwar confirms Aug 11 special Dewan Rakyat sitting to discuss TH RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has confirmed that a special Dewan Rakyat sitting to discuss the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) will be held on Aug 11.
The sitting will begin at 10am and continue until the afternoon.
Anwar said he had discussed the matter with Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Dr Johari Abdul, who agreed to convene the special sitting.
"Aug 11, special parliament sitting. I have discussed it, and the Dewan Rakyat Speaker has also agreed.
"It will start at 10am and continue until the afternoon," he told reporters after launching Maybank's new headquarters, Menara Merdeka Maybank, here today.
The sitting will allow members of parliament to debate the findings and recommendations of the RCI report on TH.
Earlier, the cabinet agreead to declassify and release the RCI report, which examined TH's management and operations between 2014 and 2020.
https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/nation/2026/07/1499640/tabung-haji-rci-report-declassified-fahmi
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said was tasked with liaising with the Dewan Rakyat Speaker to determine the date of the special sitting.
https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/nation/2026/07/1499688/pm-wants-tabung-haji-rci-findings-debated-special-dewan-rakyat-sitting
The RCI found that TH faced financial weaknesses linked to high hibah payments, investment risks, accounting issues and governance shortcomings.
Among its findings, the commission said TH should have recorded a RM1.4 billion loss in 2017 instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported in its financial statements after taking into account impairment losses and other adjustments.
The RCI also identified governance weaknesses, including broad ministerial powers over appointments, overlapping roles among directors and senior management, and concerns over political influence.
It recommended strengthening TH's governance framework through clearer criteria for board appointments, limiting active politicians from holding board positions, and improving oversight mechanisms.
The commission also proposed separating the responsibilities of the minister responsible for religious affairs, who would oversee haj matters, and the finance minister, who would oversee financial management, funds and investments.
Other recommendations included conducting forensic audits into past investments, ensuring hibah payments are based on audited financial statements, strengthening audit oversight and improving the institution's professional management.
The RCI maintained that TH should remain a single institution, saying its weaknesses could be addressed through governance and operational reforms rather than major structural changes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asyraf Wajdi: Tabung Haji RCI report debate will ensure accountability
Article:
PORT DICKSON: The tabling of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) in Parliament for debate will ensure that all parties involved are held accountable.
Welcoming the release of the report, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the party had, from the outset, called for the establishment of an RCI to investigate all allegations raised against Tabung Haji.
"The best course of action, as with other RCIs such as the Felda RCI, is for it to be debated in Parliament so that everyone involved is held accountable.
"Most importantly, no one should escape responsibility. Alhamdulillah, this is what we have been calling for all along.
"Six years ago, when I was Umno Youth chief, we were among the earliest to call for an RCI to investigate all the allegations made by the opposition regarding Tabung Haji.
"We asked that the investigation cover not only the period up to 2020, but also examine how the so-called recovery process was carried out, including the sale of assets.
"Was everything truly conducted in accordance with the requirements of the restructuring process and other relevant procedures?" he said after attending a Barisan Nasional public ceramah programme for the Chuah state constituency here.
Asyraf Wajdi said all findings disclosed in the report should be debated in Parliament.
He said the public might question why the report was released while campaigning for the Negri Sembilan state election was ongoing.
However, he said Umno hoped action would be taken if any wrongdoing was proven.
"It should not be merely about making allegations, playing on sentiment or creating negative perceptions. That is unhealthy for Malay and Islamic institutions in terms of the continuity and sustainability of the organisation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PDC to develop Batu Kawan Industrial Park 2 after failed tender rounds
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Development Corporation (PDC) will develop the Batu Kawan Industrial Park 2 project itself after three requests for proposals and tender exercises failed.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the decision was made by the PDC board on July 20, allowing the agency to have full control over the development of the strategic industrial park.
He said the approximately 1,003-acre site at Ladang Byram, which is now fully owned by PDC, would be developed in phases based on market demand.
After three unsuccessful rounds of requests for proposals and tenders, the PDC board decided to undertake the development of the area itself, he said.
"We will have full control over the development, which will be carried out in phases according to market requirements," he told newsmen after attending the Malaysian International Chamber of Commerce and Industry 2026 annual luncheon dialogue here today.
Also present was PDC chief executive officer Datuk Abdul Latiff Abd Aziz.
Chow said PDC had yet to focus on marketing the industrial park or securing investors as its immediate priority was to complete site preparation works.
He said Batu Kawan Industrial Park 2 was expected to be offered to investors around 2030, subject to the progress of infrastructure and site preparation works.
"The land is not ready yet. Until it is ready, we cannot offer it to investors. Besides site preparation, the construction of a bridge linking the area will also be an important component to improve accessibility, although the existing access via Changkat can still be used," he added.
It was reported in May that
PDC defended its rejection
of an RM818 million bid by an IJM-Aspen-Mettiz Capital consortium to develop 559 acres in Ladang Byram/Changkat, citing a potential RM294 million cost exposure for the corporation.
Separately, Chow said the development of about 80 acres on Jerejak Island by Uda Holdings Bhd was expected to begin after a bridge linking Queensbay to the island is completed in 2029.
He said the bridge formed part of the approvals granted several years ago to facilitate the private-sector development.
"The development will only involve about 80 acres, not the entire Jerejak Island, and it is a private-sector initiative that has obtained the necessary development approvals over the past few years," he said.
Chow said the project on Jerejak Island was expected to take between three and four years to complete after the bridge becomes operational.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-Tabung Haji CEO questions silence after RCI report emerges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chief executive officer Datuk Nik Mohd Hasyudeen Yusoff has taken aim at critics following the declassification of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into the institution's management and operations.
Hasyudeen said critics had been quick to react to unproven allegations but remained silent when facts emerged.
"I understand the thinking in certain WhatsApp groups; they become noisy when allegations without evidence surface, but fall silent when the facts come to light," he said in a Facebook post today.
He did not specify the allegations or groups he was referring to.
The RCI report examined Hasyudeen's removal as TH chief executive officer on May 5, 2021, months before his extended contract was due to expire on Aug 31.
It found that the minister had invoked Section 6(5) of the Tabung Haji Act 1995 to terminate the appointments of Hasyudeen and then TH chairman Tan Sri Md Nor Md Yusof before their terms ended, without giving reasons.
The commission concluded that both men had served TH well and were overseeing improvements at the institution, adding that their sudden removal had disrupted the reform process.
It recommended that the minister's power to revoke board appointments without explanation be removed from the Act.
It also recommended that any proposal to terminate a board member's appointment be referred to an independent committee or advisory body to be established.
The commission added that any proposed termination should be supported by reasonable grounds before the appointment was revoked.
It has recommended barring active
politicians
from serving as the institution's chairman, board members or directors of its subsidiaries, saying appointments should instead be based on professional qualifications and expertise.
Separately, speaking at the launch of Maybank's new headquarters, Menara Merdeka Maybank, here today, Hasyudeen said TH had been built on a strong foundation.
He said the institution, established by renowned academician and economist Royal Professor Ungku Abdul Aziz, had served hundreds of thousands of haj pilgrims.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Israeli strikes kill three in Gaza, including two children, amid new ceasefire talks
Article:
CAIRO: Israeli strikes killed at least three people, including two children, in the Gaza Strip on Thursday, health officials said, as mediators held new talks with Hamas leaders to work towards full implementation of a US-brokered Gaza peace plan.
Medics said an Israeli airstrike on a tent encampment in Khan Younis, south of the enclave, killed a man and an eight-year-old girl.
In the Bureij refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip, an Israeli airstrike hit a house killing an 18-month-old child and wounding at least eight people, medics said.
The Israeli military said both strikes targeted Hamas fighters.
The latest deaths add to a toll of more than 1,200 Palestinians, mostly civilians, killed by Israeli attacks since the ceasefire took effect, according to Gaza health officials.
Hamas does not usually disclose its losses.
The truce halted full-scale fighting but has not ended near-daily Israeli strikes. Four Israeli soldiers have been killed by fighters in Gaza over the same period.
In Cairo, Hamas leaders were holding talks with mediators from Egypt, Qatar and Turkiye, over the implementation of the second phase of President Donald Trump's Gaza plan, as presented to them by his Board of Peace, that oversees its implementation.
The plan called for a surge in humanitarian aid, governance by a civilian Palestinian administration, the disarmament of Hamas, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza and the deployment of an international force to help maintain security.
But progress has stalled in previous months.
On Thursday, a Hamas official said the group was coming with a "positive and good" response, yet he didn't say whether the group has agreed to fully disarm — a key sticking point in the talks over the past four months.
Hamas wants Israel to commit to ending attacks on Gaza and withdrawing its forces.
Sources close to Hamas said the group was willing to "confine and store" heavy weapons under a Palestinian body, not hand it over to Israel. Hamas didn't comment on that.
It is also not yet clear what would be the fate of light or personal weapons or whether the new Hamas stance would be accepted by Israel and the Board of Peace.
The Board of Peace declined immediate comment on the Cairo talks.
Israel wants Hamas to cede power completely in Gaza and to fully disarm.
Hamas dissolved a de facto Gaza government last month but kept a caretaking body to maintain the provision of vital services to residents.
Israel effectively controls an estimated 64 per cent of the tiny coastal Gaza Strip, bombed to ruins by Israel's two-year military assault that followed a 2023 Hamas attack on southern Israel.
Nearly all of Gaza's two million people now live on a sliver of land on the coast, mainly in makeshift tents or damaged buildings and facing dire living conditions.
